## Original parcel criteria, closed acreage bounds and report editions

For parcel studies, `source_tools.parcel_criteria.prepare` derives a retained criterion table from the selected original source layers. New operations default to `settings.spatial_criteria_basis="whole_original_parcel"`: hydric soils, sensitive riparian area, stream lengths and the other spatial parcel criteria use the complete original parcel. An explicit `"reporting_parcel"` selection records the reporting-boundary adaptation. Full parcel size and protected-land interpretation retain their own original geometry; land-cover and floodplain-development choices remain independently recorded. Native export and portfolio mass still use their original reporting support.

The table binds its exact parcel source, native ID/layer/filter, reporting boundary or native grid, original source bodies, `geometry_context` and `metric_geometry`. Reusing it in a point study checks that geometry identity. Equal parcel ID text from another source edition cannot silently reuse a different area's measurements. See [the geometry contract](../source_tools/PARCEL_CRITERIA_GEOMETRY.md) and [source builder](../source_tools/PARCEL_CRITERIA.md).

A hydric or sensitive-riparian acreage interval has closed lower and upper endpoints. The lower endpoint is the positively mapped area; the upper endpoint adds the part of the selected parcel geometry unresolved by actual source certainty coverage. Fully hydric and fully nonhydric map units can establish certainty under the default hydric interpretation; mixed or unknown units keep unresolved area. The canonical acreage remains null while the interval is nondegenerate. A criterion receives exact points when every value in that interval receives the same published contribution. The practice total still requires all contributions to be determined and its prerequisite to be true.

The source rules are Lake Keowee Watershed Plan (2020), Table 31 and Appendix D: sensitive riparian acreage on printed page 139, hydric acreage on page 140 and full parcel size on page 142. The published sensitive-riparian footprint combines the retained variable riparian layer with the surface-water buffer. An observed component contributes a lower limit while a missing component remains part of the upper limit. [Original plan](https://www.des.sc.gov/sites/des/files/Documents/BOW/WaterQuality/WPLakeKeowee.pdf). See [acreage intervals](../source_tools/PARCEL_CRITERIA_INTERVALS.md) for exact data and scoring fields.

Original soils and one-percent floodplain acquisition is available through `source_tools.soil_floodplain_sources`. A selected study queries its reporting geometry together with full original selected-parcel extensions. The capture reuses compatible original soil geometry, retains each source family independently, imports the original and criterion editions, and returns `parcel_criteria_selection` for the existing builder. Original HTTP bodies, component attributes, native IDs, query geometry and certainty coverage stay with those editions. See [source acquisition](../source_tools/SOIL_FLOODPLAIN_SOURCES.md).

The existing export command now creates a presentation edition over verified saved candidates, geometries and selected plan IDs. It keeps the original study and plan artifacts intact. HTML, CSV and GeoPackage expose full and reporting acreage, prerequisite state, exact or bounded points, criterion geometry and source references. Supplemental criterion/value tables, original criterion bytes and a source register accompany `presentation.json`; its file descriptors are bound by the ordinary portable export manifest. Reopening an export reads the original measurements and saved decision. [Report contract](CONSERVATION_REPORTS.md).

## Source-derived acreage intervals and presentation continuity

The original selected candidate remains the consumer's authoritative scientific record. A point candidate's `point_score.metric_bounds` retains closed acreage endpoints, observed positive area, unresolved area, certainty coverage, actual geometry basis and source references. `point_score.metric_values` keeps an unresolved exact acreage null. Individual `score_components` retain their known/possible contribution and whether the whole interval determined exact points. A complete point score can therefore coexist with a bounded acreage measurement.

A true practice prerequisite and equal total contribution bounds determine an applicable exact practice score. Missing and false prerequisites retain their own states. Downstream implementation or monitoring records can display those states directly while preserving the original `unit_key`, native ID and source selection. Published points remain parcel-priority quantities; physical annual mass and selected-union quantities retain their original separate fields.

Builder-produced criterion metadata records `spatial_criteria_basis` and per-field `metric_geometry`. New source derivations default to the whole original parcel; reporting-boundary criteria are an explicit retained adaptation. Parcel size, protected-land, land-cover, floodplain-development and native export bases can differ deliberately and are recorded separately. The source table binds the exact original parcel/reporting context, so a matching ID string alone is insufficient to substitute another geometry edition. The full metadata and original criterion source remain in the retained study and source assets.

`conservation.export_packet` now binds an additional presentation edition to the same verified candidate and geometry files and saved selected IDs. It retains prior study/plan file descriptors and creates current HTML, CSV/GIS and criterion/source supplements in its own export directory. Consumers reopening an older saved plan keep the original source and decision identities while receiving the current readable presentation. The full working archive continues through the ordinary Workspace backup/restore path. See [CONSERVATION_REPORTS.md](CONSERVATION_REPORTS.md), [PARCEL_CRITERIA_GEOMETRY.md](../source_tools/PARCEL_CRITERIA_GEOMETRY.md) and [PARCEL_CRITERIA_INTERVALS.md](../source_tools/PARCEL_CRITERIA_INTERVALS.md).

## Original soils and floodplains to a saved point study

Open the original parcel study and choose **Acquire soils and floodplains**. Select soils, one-percent floodplain geography or both, and record the hydric interpretation. The acquisition domain includes the reporting geometry and every selected full-parcel extension. Reuse an existing compatible original source or the original soil capture directory when available. The source pipeline requests the uncovered part of that same domain and retains original responses and native identities.

The operation records family progress, retained original/criterion source editions, source coverage and prepared builder bindings. Reopen it from the Conservation acquisition list or its retained task. Resume uses that same operation ID and preserved source requests. A completed family supplies usable criteria while an unfinished family continues independently.

Choose **Prepare parcel criteria** from the actual saved acquisition, selecting the intended **Source criterion geometry**. The existing `conservation.criteria.prepare` action consumes `source_operation_id` and the returned original `parcel_criteria_selection`; an optional `settings.spatial_criteria_basis` chooses `whole_original_parcel` or `reporting_parcel`. The queued builder imports the resulting JSON/CSV/GIS table. **Use prepared parcel criteria** reopens the originating study geometry and selects that actual table in the point-study form.

Build the published-practice inventory. Candidate details show each metric's exact value or closed acreage interval, geometry basis and original source, followed by each published criterion's points or contribution range and the practice prerequisite. Exact points can be resolved by a bounded acreage when its entire interval falls in the same published step. The exact acreage remains bounded until source coverage determines it.

Save the chosen land through the ordinary manual, ranked or optimized portfolio workflow. The plan retains the same selected IDs and its actual full/reporting union geometry. The soil and floodplain source guide, parcel geometry guide and interval guide provide the complete callable and source contracts: [SOIL_FLOODPLAIN_SOURCES.md](../source_tools/SOIL_FLOODPLAIN_SOURCES.md), [PARCEL_CRITERIA_GEOMETRY.md](../source_tools/PARCEL_CRITERIA_GEOMETRY.md), and [PARCEL_CRITERIA_INTERVALS.md](../source_tools/PARCEL_CRITERIA_INTERVALS.md).

## Review and preserve an optimizer decision

The completed-study optimizer offers geographic context, available native quantities and complete applicable published-practice points. Review its actual candidate inventory, explicit weights, source/native coverage, resource limits, cost availability, solver status, original selected IDs and named preference results. Physical comparisons retain their selected original alternative and common support. Published-point density, when chosen, divides parcel priority points by actual reporting hectares and keeps that denominator visible.

Saving an already reviewed preview submits only its original completed `preview_task_id`. The provider reads that task in the same workspace, and the model checks the complete recorded analysis, source study, original candidate/geometry files and selected IDs. It saves that exact decision and original normalized request. A new-spec optimization request remains a separate explicit calculation through the same maintained save action. The ordinary plan service computes the selected geometry union and physical summary.

The saved decision reopens through the original optimized-plan/analysis routes. Its export includes the complete candidate inventory and original decision analysis. The saved portfolio continues to **Create land-cover scenario** and the matching native experiment workflow described above. [Optimization guide](CONSERVATION_OPTIMIZATION.md).

## Read and reopen the full criterion report

Export the candidate inventory or saved portfolio through its existing control. The report separates full original parcel acreage, reporting acreage and the geometry used by each criterion. It displays prerequisite status, exact points or possible point range, and the original criterion contributions without converting those points into pollutant mass. Acreage endpoints retain their exact closed-bound meaning.

The ZIP includes the normal editable GIS and candidate tables, `criterion-contributions.csv`, `criterion-values.csv`, `criterion-scores.json`, source-register JSON/CSV, the retained original criterion table and `presentation.json`. Original source URLs, editions, selected fields and file hashes accompany the result. Larger reports retain the complete machine-readable inventory alongside the clearly identified preview in HTML.

A current presentation is created from the same verified saved measurements and selected plan IDs. Earlier study/plan artifact hashes remain intact. Reopen the same saved study or portfolio after restarting the operator; use the ordinary Workspace backup/restore workflow to carry the sources, queued operation records, criteria and decisions to another receiving copy. [Report and export contract](../model/CONSERVATION_REPORTS.md).

## Interval-derived points and original source reporting

A published-method objective uses an exact applicable practice total: the retained lower and upper contribution sums must agree, the prerequisite must be true, and the original point total must equal the candidate score. A numeric acreage can remain a closed interval while all values in it receive the same published points. Incomplete, inapplicable or unknown-prerequisite totals retain their original state and do not satisfy a positive published-point weight. Required native export criteria also retain their original selected pollutant output and coverage threshold.

The full original candidate is preserved in each analysis row and CSV record, including `point_score.metric_bounds`, metric/source bindings and criterion contributions. The request binds the published definition, original table and interpretation. The full source-study selection remains in the analysis. Choosing per-reporting-hectare explicitly divides those original parcel points by actual reporting area; the actual whole-parcel or reporting criterion geometry remains separately recorded.

Decision export calls the original Conservation report/export service before adding the retained optimization files. Current packets therefore include the exact/bounded criterion tables, source register, original criterion bytes and presentation identity as well as the decision analysis. The report describes the actual saved optimizer choice and solver result; manual and greedy ranked plans retain their respective selection meaning. See [CONSERVATION_REPORTS.md](../model/CONSERVATION_REPORTS.md).

## Original source and criterion continuation

The maintained Conservation descriptor registers `conservation.sources.capture` once beside the original seven actions. A new acquisition supplies `spec`; a continuation supplies the original `operation_id`. The provider queues the existing soils/FEMA acquisition module and exposes the retained operation through `/api/conservation/source-capture?operation_id=ID`. Overview adds the saved source acquisitions alongside criteria operations, studies and portfolios.

The existing `conservation.criteria.prepare` action also accepts `source_operation_id`. It consumes that actual capture's returned `parcel_criteria_selection` and optionally merges the explicitly selected `settings.spatial_criteria_basis`. The two choices are `whole_original_parcel` and `reporting_parcel`. Completed source families remain available through their original editions while another family resumes. The prepared table records its originating study and exact parcel/reporting geometry; using it restores that selection before published points are built.

Receive the full acquisition, criterion, published-method, reporting, scenario and optimization cohort together. The [operator journey](CONSERVATION.md) connects actual sources, bounded acreage, published points, saved selection, original native scenario and report export. [CONSERVATION_REPORTS.md](../model/CONSERVATION_REPORTS.md) describes retained presentation editions and complete source/criterion tables. Existing source identities, task history and portable Workspace receiving remain the host's shared surface.

Saving a reviewed optimizer preview uses the original completed task ID. Its provider verifies the same workspace/action/state, and its scientific model verifies the recorded analysis against the original study and candidate/geometry inventories before saving the exact selected units. The complete decision then travels through the original Conservation plan and export interfaces.
